## Session 120 (2026-07-27) — pursued NEXT.md's branch (a) allocator hunt, found a real (but not causal here) asymmetric-free alias bug, then a sharper source-confirmed pattern (corrupted scan indices always exceed the live allocation's own voiceCount), and along the way discovered a serious, undocumented regen-pipeline reliability bug that produced two false leads before being caught

**Branch (a) grep hunt (no soak needed to start, per NEXT.md).** Grepped
`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/*.c` for every store to the `-0x6908`
global (`musyxMixActiveVoices`'s voice-array base, reloaded fresh every
scan) and found exactly one site anywhere in the tree:
`allocateSongChannelArray` (`funcs_23.c`), which stores the *same*
`rs_malloc` pointer into **two** adjacent globals, `-0x6904` and
`-0x6908` (`0x801496FC`/`0x801496F8`), and a matching single store to
`-0x6900` (voice count) right before the `rs_malloc` call. Grepped
`rs_free` call sites and found `shutdownAudioEngine` (`funcs_24.c`,
reached via `shutdownMusyXEngine`) frees the `-0x6904` copy but **never
touches `-0x6908`** — a genuine, source-confirmed asymmetric-free /
dangling-alias bug in the original game's own compiled code (not a
recomp artifact: both addresses are real N64 instruction addresses).
Landed `ROGUESQ_LOG_SONG_ARRAY_LIFECYCLE=1` (logs the alloc's
voiceCount+pointer, and at the `shutdownAudioEngine` free site, the
value being freed plus a fresh read of `-0x6908` for comparison).

**Two soaks (`songlifecycle1`, `songlifecycle2`, same shape, ~150s
`start_only`/`HOLD_S=30`) directly refute this as the cause of the
observed corruption in this code path**: `[song-array-alloc]` fired 6
times (voiceCounts 20/17/16/15/18/18, 3 distinct pointers, one reused
3x by the allocator — expected heap-reuse behaviour), but
`[shutdown-audio-free]` fired **0/2** — `shutdownAudioEngine` never ran
in either soak, so `-0x6908` was never left dangling by this mechanism
in these runs. The alias bug is real and independently worth fixing
some day, but it is not what produced either soak's corruption.

**Sharper finding, reproduced 2/2 independently:** in both soaks, every
`[voice-active-gate-nz]` corrupted-byte hit has an `idx` that **exceeds
the currently-live allocation's own `voiceCount`** — burst 1: idx
16,17 against a `voiceCount=15` allocation (base arithmetic
`base − idx*0x88` solves to exactly that allocation's own pointer,
`0x801714D0`, confirmed independently from 4+ data points via linear
stride-fitting, not just one); burst 2: idx 19-31 against a
`voiceCount=18` allocation (same exact-match technique, same pointer).
The scanned base address is the *current, valid* allocation both
times, not a stale one from an older `[song-array-alloc]` event — so
this is not the dangling-alias bug above, and not simply "reading a
freed block" either. The loop bound comes from a fresh `-0x6900` read
every iteration (`funcs_24.c` ~0x80090F44), which — per the single-
store-site grep above — is written by the *same* `allocateSongChannelArray`
call, at the *same* time, as `-0x6908`'s pointer. Why the scan is
permitted past that value is not yet resolved.

**Attempted to close this directly and found a bug in my own
instrument first.** Added `count=`/`arrayBase=` fields to the existing
`[voice-active-gate-nz]` log, reading `-0x6900`/`-0x6908` fresh at the
exact corruption instant via `MEM_HU(0x80150000, -0X6900)` /
`MEM_W(0x80150000, -0X6908)`. First attempt passed the bare 32-bit
literal `0x80150000` directly instead of the codebase's own
`ctx->rN = S32(0x8015 << 16)` sign-extend-then-assign-to-`gpr` idiom —
`0x80150000` types as `unsigned int` in C (exceeds `INT_MAX`), so the
macro's internal 64-bit arithmetic zero-extends instead of
sign-extends, silently computing the wrong absolute address. This
produced `count=0x0029 arrayBase=0x72657375` — a value that looked like
a dramatic new discovery (globals themselves holding non-pointer
garbage) but was actually just reading unrelated memory consistently,
an artifact of the bug, not a game-state fact. Caught before writing
it up as a finding; fixed by using
`(gpr)(int32_t)(0X8015 << 16)` as an intermediate, matching the proven
idiom exactly. **Not yet re-soaked with the corrected version** — see
below for why.

**Major, higher-priority finding: the documented regen pipeline
(`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake`) does
not reliably produce a clean build, even when every output `.c` file is
deleted first.** While rebuilding after the S32 fix, the build failed
on `error: redefinition of label 'L_dlentry_guard_exit'` in
`funcs_3.c` — a label from s109's guard patch, applied twice. Traced
this two ways:
1. First occurrence: ran the full documented order *without* deleting
   `RecompiledFuncs/*.c` first. Deleting the single stale file and
   re-running `N64Recomp` alone (no fixup yet) produced a byte-for-byte
   pristine file (0 `dlentry` occurrences) — proving `N64Recomp` will
   skip rewriting a `.c` file that already exists on disk, so any file
   `fixup_game_funcs.py` has ever patched stays patched forever unless
   manually deleted, and re-running fixup on it stacks a second copy of
   every patch whose anchor text survives its own insertion (the anchor
   is the original, unmodified instruction sequence — patches only
   insert *after* it, so it still matches). This is a sharper root
   cause than s102's "fixup isn't idempotent": it's `N64Recomp`, not
   `fixup_game_funcs.py`, that's the unreliable half.
2. Fixed by deleting **all 45** `RecompiledFuncs/funcs_*.c` before
   every `N64Recomp` invocation (new helper:
   `tools/agent/regen_n64recomp.sh`, also works around the headless
   permission-prefix-match wall for `cd .../N64Recomp && ./build/N64Recomp ...`
   commands, rule 10's family of issues). This worked once (confirmed
   every patch report line reads exactly `x1`, including several that
   had apparently been silently *not* re-applying for who knows how
   many past sessions — `funcs_23.c: audio gate patched x3`,
   `funcs_24.c: musyxKeyOnVoice div-traps patched x8`, etc., that never
   showed up in earlier "clean" runs' reports).
3. **But the very next full-clean cycle (delete-all → regen → fixup →
   build) reproduced the exact same duplicate-label failure again**,
   this time in *two* files (`funcs_3.c` and `funcs_40.c`'s
   `L_hangarbay_guard_exit`), and a `grep` audit found `funcs_23.c` and
   `funcs_24.c`'s newer diagnostic patches *also* silently doubled
   (non-erroring, since each patch's `{ }` block is its own C scope —
   only patches that also declare a bare function-scoped `goto` label
   surface as a compile error; the rest just silently double-log).
   Ruled out cmake auto-invoking `fixup_game_funcs.py` a second time
   (no reference to it anywhere under `build/`) and duplicate path
   enumeration via `glob()` (checked directly, 45 unique paths, no
   dupes). **Root cause not identified** — deleting all files first
   is necessary but evidently not sufficient; whatever's caching/
   restoring already-patched content survives file deletion.
   Manually deduplicated the two compile-blocking labels
   (`funcs_3.c`, `funcs_40.c`) directly in the generated files to
   restore a working build; left `funcs_23.c`/`funcs_24.c`'s silently-
   doubled (harmless-to-correctness, just double-printing) diagnostic
   blocks as-is given time spent.

**Why this matters more than the M3 question it interrupted:** this
casts reasonable doubt on any past session's soak conclusions that
relied on a patch landed and soaked without an explicit post-build
duplication audit (most of s90 onward, once multi-patch fixup runs
became routine) — a doubled diagnostic wouldn't change underlying game
behavior (still block-scoped, side-effect-free logging), so crash/
stability conclusions are very likely unaffected, but any conclusion
resting on an exact *count* or *first-occurrence* value from a log
(several sessions' `n=` heartbeat-style reasoning, including this
session's own idx-exceeds-count arithmetic derived from `idx=`/`base=`
register reads — unaffected, since those are plain `ctx->rN` reads with
no address macro involved, not vulnerable to this specific class of
duplication) should be treated as provisional until re-verified against
a build whose patch report has been grepped for anything other than
`x1`/an intentional multiplicity.

Both soaks also reproduced the already-well-characterized `do_rom_read`
SIGSEGV (byte-identical stack trace to s85-s119) shortly after each
corruption burst — 2/2 temporal co-occurrence, consistent with but not
proof of the s85 "shared corruption race" framing (s118 already refuted
byte-identity between this family and the voice corruption).
`thr-resume bad_total=0` both soaks (control held).

## Session 121 (2026-07-27) — clean regen with zero patch duplication (contradicts s120's implicit "always duplicates" framing), then the corrected voice-active-gate soak overturns s120's own "idx always exceeds voiceCount" conclusion and exposes a cross-thread log-ordering confound in the methodology used to derive it

**Step 1: regen-pipeline audit (NEXT.md, gate before trusting any soak).**
Ran the full delete-all → `make_elf.py` → `regen_n64recomp.sh` → `fixup_
game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build` cycle exactly as documented. Result:
**zero duplication this time** — every patch report line read `x1`
except the two intentionally-multi-site patches (`funcs_23.c` audio gate
`x3`, `funcs_24.c` musyxKeyOnVoice div-traps `x8`, both matching known
multiplicity), and both s120 hand-fixed labels (`L_dlentry_guard_exit`,
`L_hangarbay_guard_exit`) came out as single declarations from a fresh,
undoctored regen. Build: exit 0, no `error:`, only the pre-existing
pointer-sign warning class. **This means the duplication bug s120 found
is intermittent, not guaranteed on every clean cycle** — s120's
"reproduced twice in a row" should not be read as "always reproduces";
treat every future regen as needing its own audit (per NEXT.md step 2),
not as a foregone conclusion either way.

**Step 2: songlifecycle3 soak — the 3rd and last allowed soak in this
family (rule 8).** Ran the exact NEXT.md-prescribed command
(`ROGUESQ_LOG_SONG_ARRAY_LIFECYCLE=1 ROGUESQ_LOG_VOICE_ACTIVE_GATE=1
PROBE_MODE=start_only HOLD_S=30`, tag `songlifecycle3`). This soak used
the sign-extension-bug-fixed instrument (confirmed sane: `count=0x0012`
(18) / `arrayBase=0x801714D0`, both real values — unlike `songlifecycle2`,
which is now confirmed in this session to be the buggy read:
`count=0x0029 arrayBase=0x72657375` ("resu" as ASCII), i.e. garbage,
consistent with s120's own bug report).

Two bursts fired (19 lines total, `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/songlifecycle3/
run.log`):
- **Burst 1** (n=68910-68965): `idx=0x10,0x11` (16,17), `count=0x0012`
  (18), `arrayBase=0x801714D0`. **16 and 17 do not exceed 18** — this
  directly contradicts s120's own characterization of this exact burst
  ("idx 16-17 vs voiceCount=15", i.e. exceeding count). Cross-checked
  against `[song-array-alloc]` log order: at the moment burst 1 fires,
  the alloc line immediately preceding it (same `ptr=0x801714D0`) reads
  `voiceCount=15`, and the matching `voiceCount=18` alloc line for that
  same pointer appears **18 lines later in the file** — i.e. by raw log
  order, the count register instrument read a value (18) that "hadn't
  been written yet" relative to the allocator's own log line.
- **Burst 2** (n=127202+): `idx=0x06,0x10` (6,16), `count=0x0012` (18),
  `arrayBase=0x801714D0`, firing after *two* consecutive `voiceCount=18`
  allocs at that same pointer — count now genuinely matches the
  live allocation, and **idx (6,16) still does not exceed count (18)**.

**Conclusion: in this soak, no corrupted scan index ever exceeded a
directly-read, sane loop-bound register — refuting s120's central
"idx always exceeds voiceCount" claim.** That claim was never based on
a live read of the loop bound (this instrument didn't have the field
yet when s120 wrote it); it was derived by eyeballing the temporally-
nearest `[song-array-alloc]` line in the log file. Burst 1 here shows
exactly why that method is unsound: the audio-tick thread's `[voice-
active-gate-nz]` print and the allocator's `[song-array-alloc]` print
have no shared sequence number, so file line order across the two
independent log call sites is not a valid proxy for real chronological
order (most likely ordinary stdout-buffering skew between threads, not
evidence of anything exotic — boring explanation preferred and nothing
here rules it out). **Generalizable methodology gap**: every s117-120
conclusion that compared an `idx`/`base` value against a *nearby but
not sequence-tied* `voiceCount` log line inherits this same risk and
should be treated as provisional, not just this one instrument.

With `count=`/`arrayBase=` both confirmed sane (not the "BSS/global
corruption, second corruption region" branch NEXT.md flagged as the
other possible outcome), the mystery **fully reframes back to content,
not bounds**: the byte dump at every firing (`bytes:` lines) shows the
same recognizable ASCII/string-table fragments s118 already
characterized independently (`expl_tex2`, `x10`/`x11`, `explo_te`,
"lecfik_e" etc. — texture/asset-name-shaped strings), now at indices
(6, 16, 17) that are provably *inside* the live allocation's bounds.
**Two independent lines of evidence now agree**: s118's widened dump
(different session, different instrument) and this session's bounds-
checked read both show string-table content sitting at legitimate
voice-array slots. The open question is unchanged in kind but sharper
in scope: **what writes/aliases string-table data into `voice+0x0`
at real, in-bounds array offsets** — not "does the scan run out of
bounds" (closed, no) and not "is the loop-bound global itself corrupted"
(closed, no, this run).

Per rule 8, this was the 3rd consecutive `songlifecycle*` soak — but it
*was* discriminating (overturns s120's framing), so no forced pivot is
needed on procedural grounds; the substantive next step is naturally a
different one anyway (find the aliasing/name-table write), not a 4th
idx-vs-count soak.

Did not re-touch the `shutdownAudioEngine`/alias hypothesis (already
2/2 refuted, s120) or hypothesis (b) (`musyxInitVoiceFromSample`,
closed s119) per NEXT.md's do-not list.

## Session 122 (2026-07-27) — source-read refutes literal H1 for the voice+0x0 mystery (allocateSongChannelArray explicitly zero-inits every live voice slot's byte 0), pivots to a new address-coincidence instrument for H2, and incidentally catches a 2nd occurrence of the already-catalogued 18th crash class

**Step 1: source read before instrumenting (NEXT.md's own prescribed
first move).** Read `allocateSongChannelArray` (`funcs_23.c`) in full
around the single `rs_malloc` call that establishes both `-0x6904` and
`-0x6908` (the voice-array base, s120). Found a loop (`L_8008F118`,
guest `0x8008F118`-`0x8008F168`) that runs unconditionally for every
index `0..voiceCount-1` (from the freshly-read `-0x6900` half-word) and
writes `MEM_B(0x0, base+idx*0x88) = 0` — i.e. an explicit, per-voice
zero-init of exactly the byte NEXT.md's H1/H2 split is about, executed
synchronously inside the allocator function itself, before the pointer
is stored anywhere else or used by any other subsystem. This closes
NEXT.md's own contingency ("if it already memsets the buffer, that
changes where to hook") — it does, functionally, for byte 0 specifically
(the loop also touches offsets 0x84/0x85, unrelated to this question).

**Consequence:** literal H1 ("stale rs_malloc leftover persisting
unmodified through use") is refuted at the source level, not just
weakened — `voice+0x0` is provably `0` for every live index immediately
after every call to `allocateSongChannelArray`, regardless of what
`rs_malloc` handed back. Whatever content s118/s121 observed later must
be written *after* this zero-init completes, by something else. This
did not require a rebuild or a soak; it is a single-source (code
reading) but deterministic result — the code either has this loop or it
doesn't, and it does.

**Step 2: pivoted to NEXT.md's H2 branch** ("grep for name-table-
populating functions... check whether its buffer's address ever
coincides with the voice array's `arrayBase`"). `main_overlay.txt`
names `loadExplosionTextures` (`0x8006108C`) as the likely producer of
the `explo_tex` strings s118 found; it delegates to the generic asset
loader `loadAssetAndIterateSubchunks` (`0x80054EF0`, `funcs_11.c`,
4 known callers per the symbol comment: `allocAndInitParticlePool`,
`handleHUD`, `loadExplosionTextures`, `loadTopCloudsAsset`), which calls
the **same** `rs_malloc` allocator as the voice array for its DMA
target buffer.

Landed `ROGUESQ_LOG_ASSET_ALLOC=1` (`_asset_alloc_patch`, `funcs_11.c`,
right after the first `rs_malloc(size, align=4)` call in
`loadAssetAndIterateSubchunks` returns) logging the buffer pointer
(`ctx->r22`), requested size (`ctx->r20`), and the caller's return
address read back off the stack slot saved at function entry
(`MEM_W(0x64, ctx->r29)` — not `ctx->r31`, which is clobbered by this
function's own internal `jal`s by that point).

Full delete-all → `make_elf.py` → `regen_n64recomp.sh` →
`fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build` cycle: clean, every patch report
line `x1` (or its documented multiplicity: audio gate `x3`, musyxKeyOnVoice
div-traps `x8`), no duplication this cycle, build exit 0 (new
`loadAssetAndIterateSubchunks rs_malloc diagnostic patched x1` line
confirmed the new patch landed exactly once).

**Soak 1 (`assetalloc1`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_SONG_ARRAY_LIFECYCLE=1
ROGUESQ_LOG_ASSET_ALLOC=1 PROBE_MODE=start_only HOLD_S=30`):**
`[song-array-alloc]` fired 6x (`ptr` cycling `0x80169460`/`0x801714D0`/
`0x8018D4A0`, `voiceCount` 15-20). `[asset-alloc]` fired 6x, **all with
the same `ptr=0x8062B850`** despite very different sizes (76960, 72900,

not a result.

**Soak 2 (`assetalloc2`, adds `ROGUESQ_LOG_VOICE_ACTIVE_GATE=1` to fix

## Session 123 (2026-07-27) — source-pinned the 18th crash class's real fault site (nearest-symbol attribution was wrong by a whole function), landed and soaked a guard following the established family pattern, clean negative control, no regression

Followed NEXT.md exactly: source-read `submitSceneNodeRender` before
instrumenting, per this family's own established convention (12th/16th/
17th classes all got the same treatment on their 2nd recurrence).

**Step 1 — resolved the nearest-symbol address.** `symbol_files/
main_overlay.txt` places `heapFreeListDequeue` at `0x8000CFD4`. The 2nd
occurrence's backtrace offset (`+12704` = `0x31A0`) resolves to
`0x8000CFD4 + 0x31A0 = 0x80010174`. That address is **not** inside
`heapFreeListDequeue` at all — confirmed by `grep`ping the recompiled
tree (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c`), `0x80010174` is a label
(`L_80010174`) inside `submitSceneNodeRender`'s own body, a wholly
different function that merely happens to sit at a higher address in
the same overlay. This is a sharper instance of NEXT.md's own warning
("nearest exported symbol is known-imprecise for this family") — not
just imprecise by a few instructions, imprecise by an entire function.

**Step 2 — read the actual code at that label.** It is a singly-linked-
list "find the tail" walk, fed by `findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry`'s return
value (copied into `$a0`/`ctx->r4` just before):

    L_80010174:
        v1 = *v1;      // 0x80010174 -- the crash PC, exactly
        v0 = *v1;      // 0x80010178
        if (v0 != 0) goto L_80010174;

A **new shape** for this family: not a fixed-table lookup (12th/16th
class) and not a single arg-pointer deref checked once at entry (9th/
10th/11th class), but an **unbounded pointer-chasing loop** with zero
validation on the chased pointer (`$v1`) at any step, on any iteration.
If the node `findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry` returns is corrupt, or any
node's own first field ("next") is corrupt, the very next iteration
dereferences garbage — landing exactly on `0x80010174`, matching the
crash PC precisely (not "somewhere nearby", the literal instruction).

**Step 3 — found a safe bail-out target already in the original code.**
At `0x80010160`, when the initial `$a0` is null, the original code
already jumps to `L_800101A4`, which reloads its one live register
(`$a0`) fresh from a global list-head at `0x801163B0` — it depends on
nothing computed inside the loop. That makes it a ready-made "abandon
this relink, treat it as an empty list" reentry point, semantically
identical to what the original code already does for the null-pointer
case. Landed the guard at the top of `L_80010174` (covers both the
initial fallthrough into the loop and the loop's own back-edge, since
both pass through the label): bounds-check `U32(ctx->r3)` against the
RDRAM window (`0x80000000`-`0x80800000`, same convention as every prior
guard in this file), and `goto L_800101A4` on failure. Logs
`[scene-node-list-guard]` when `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_LIST_GUARD=1`.
Applied `U32()` truncation before the bounds compare per s99's own
postmortem (a bare 64-bit `ctx->rN` compare against 32-bit literal
bounds is a documented 100%-false-positive trap).

**Regen + build:** full delete-all → `make_elf.py` → `regen_n64recomp.sh`
→ `fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build` cycle. Patch report audited in
full: every line's multiplicity matched expectation (audio gate `x3`,
musyxKeyOnVoice div-traps `x8`, everything else `x1`), including the new
`funcs_4.c: submitSceneNodeRender free-list-walk guard patched x1` line.
Build exit 0, only pre-existing-class format warnings.

**Soak (`s123guard`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_LIST_GUARD=1
ROGUESQ_LOG_ASSET_ALLOC=1 ROGUESQ_LOG_VOICE_ACTIVE_GATE=1
PROBE_MODE=start_only HOLD_S=30`):** clean negative control —

**Offline analysis of the captured data (zero extra cost, same soak):**

**Subagent finding:** no second deref of the raw `a0`/`a1` arguments
(`ctx->r16`/`ctx->r17`) anywhere past the guard — `a1`/`ctx->r17` is
only ever used as a bitmask test (`AND 0x4000`), never as an address.
It did flag a repeated "global pointer loaded, then immediately
dereferenced with no visible check" pattern (three near-identical
free-list-pop sequences around `0x8000CC28`/`0x8000CD24`/`0x8000CE30`
and their surrounding pool-bookkeeping derefs), but explicitly rated it
PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED — its own caveat was that these looked like
internal engine free-list/queue pointers, not raw externally-supplied
arguments, and that this might be a structurally different (SDK-idiom,
safe-by-construction) pattern rather than the same corruption-race
class as the guarded site.

**Verification (direct read, lines 14435-14634 and a `ctx->r16`/`r17`
grep across the full function body):** confirmed the subagent's caveat
was the correct call, not hedging. The three flagged sites are a single
allocator idiom repeated per sub-pool: pop the head of a sentinel-based
circular free list rooted at fixed globals (`0x801163B0`
head-of-free-list, `0x801163FC`/`0x8012...-0x5824` queue-tail
bookkeeping), unlink it, and either return it or evict the smallest
live entry via `findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry` if the pool is exhausted —
the same DL-segment-buffer-pool allocator idiom used throughout the
N64 SDK's graphics task queue (sentinel node is a permanent fixture of
the list, never NULL in normal operation, by construction of the
allocator itself, not by an omitted check). Critically, `ctx->r4` is
**reloaded from the pool-head global** at 0x8000CC1C before any of the
flagged derefs — it is not the caller's original `a0` argument by that
point, and `ctx->r16` is later reassigned to `ctx->r4 + 8` (the
allocated entry's live pointer, line ~14633), not reused as the raw
external pointer either. This is categorically different from the
already-guarded site and from every other confirmed hit in this
thread family (composeNpcOrientationMatrix, updateAnimatedTexture
Streaming, static_5_800B4048, projectModelBoundsToScreen): those were
all a second deref of the SAME externally-supplied, corruption-race-
exposed pointer the first guard already existed to catch. Guarding
internal allocator bookkeeping pointers here would be scope creep past
Thread A's actual finding pattern, not a fix for a matching bug class.

the first clean audit in the Thread A series (previously 4/4 hits:
composeNpcOrientationMatrix s126; updateAnimatedTextureStreaming +
static_5_800B4048 s127; projectModelBoundsToScreen s128). Updated
running tally: **4 hits, 1 clean, out of 5 functions audited** (1 of

**Executed NEXT.md's prescribed work unit: source-read `submitSceneNodeRender`'s
non-free-list code for a 2nd unguarded pointer-chase idiom.** Found one,

**The read.** Delegated the ~2966-line source read (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/
funcs_4.c:6-2972`) to a subagent scoped to skip the already-guarded
`findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry`-return free-list-walk idiom (proven innocent of
the 18th class twice, s131/s134) and hunt for a structurally different
unguarded-pointer-chase shape. It found one, occurring twice: a pointer
(`$s1`/`ctx->r17`) loaded directly from a fixed global table (bases `-0x1758`
and `-0x1750` at guest `0x80010308`/`0x80010A1C`, indexed by the
material-group loop variable -- two separate inlined copies of the same
source loop), dereferenced immediately, surviving untouched across an
intervening free-list-walk detour (different registers), then walked as its
own "next" linked list (offset `0x0`) inside a loop (`L_8001049C`/
`L_80010A2C`) whose body dereferences `+0x4` every iteration and feeds
`heapFreeListDequeue` -- the same nearest-symbol match as the 18th crash
class, but via a completely different, previously-unaudited pointer source
than the already-guarded free-list-return-value idiom. Verified directly by
reading the regenerated source at both sites (not trusting the subagent's
report unread): confirmed `r17` is live and dereferenced at 4 distinct
points (guest `0x8001030C`/`0x80010490`/`0x8001049C`/`0x800104B0` for site 1,
and the equivalent 4 for site 2) with zero range checks anywhere in the
chain, and confirmed the intervening free-list-walk detour uses entirely
different registers (`r2`-`r4`), so it never touches or protects `r17`.

**The fix.** Landed `_mat_list_guard1_patch`/`_mat_list_guard2_patch` in
`fixup_game_funcs.py` (`funcs_4.c`-scoped), same `U32()`-before-bounds-compare
discipline as every prior guard in this series. Guarded at the single point
each table lookup's result first becomes live (before ANY dereference) --
this protects every downstream use with one check per site instead of one
per dereference. Bail targets are each site's own natural "done with this
table entry, continue the outer loop" reentry point: site 1 has a
ready-made label (`L_800104BC`) that re-derives everything it needs fresh,
so a bare `goto` suffices; site 2 has no label at the exact right spot, so
the bail inlines the same `$s0--` decrement the original code performs
immediately before falling into `L_80010CF0`, preserving outer-loop
progress so a repeat corruption can't spin on the same table entry forever.

## Session 138 (2026-07-27) — Thread B fresh-angle grep run: solved the ROM->RAM string-table mapping NEXT.md flagged as unresolved, then used it to refute the specific "static ROM literal table" candidate for the voice+0x34 aliasing source

Ran NEXT.md's exact prescribed first steps (pure source/data read, no
rebuild, no soak) for Thread B's fresh-angle grep: locate the ROM string
literals behind the asset-name fragments observed at the corrupted
`voice+0x34` reads (s118/s126: `explo_tex`/`explh_tex`/`iexpl2_tx`-shaped
strings, plus digit-suffixed/two-word fragments `explo_tex2`, `explx3`,
`x7`..`x11`, `main_n_atpt_lod`, `at_6`, `at_7`, `pilot_sd`, `xenlight`,
`xckpit`, `mat_6`, `mat_7`, `_main_0`).

**Step 1 (ROM string locate):** `strings -a -t x` over `build/rogue_squadron.z64`
found exactly one real ROM string table matching this theme, a 12-byte-stride
explosion-texture asset-name table at ROM `0x3bf70`-`0x3bfec`: `explo2_IMGS`,
`explo_tex`, `explo2hi_IMGS`, `explh_tex`, `ionexp_IMGS`, `iexplo_tx`,
`ionex2_IMGS`, `iexpl2_tx`, `smkexp_IMGS`, `sexplo_tx`, `smkexp_PAL`. A full
506k-line strings dump of the whole ROM (`-n 3`, kept at
`scratch/agent/rom_strings.txt`, gitignored) found **zero literal matches**
anywhere for `tarexex`, `main_n_atpt_lod`, `at_6`, `at_7`, or `pilot_sd` —
those specific fragments are not compile-time ROM string data at all.

**Step 2 (ROM->RAM mapping, the "genuinely unresolved unknown" NEXT.md
flagged):** solved and triple-cross-validated. `symbol_files/main_overlay.txt`'s
Strings section already lists several of this same table's neighbors with
both RAM address *and* decoded content in the comment (`strLoTx = 0x8003B404;
// ... 'lo_tx'`, `strMGold = 0x8003B418; // ... 'm_gold'`, `strMSilver =
0x8003B420; // ... 'm_silver'`) — matching them against this session's own
ROM offsets for the same strings (`lo_tx` at `0x3c004`, `m_gold` at `0x3c018`,
`m_silver` at `0x3c020`) gives an identical bias for all three pairs:
**RAM = ROM_offset + 0x7FFFF400.** Independent 2nd confirmation: read
`loadExplosionTextures` directly in `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_13.c`
(guest `0x8006108C`, matches `symbol_files/main_overlay.txt`'s own comment
naming exactly these two string pairs) and extracted the four literal RAM
addresses its two `loadAssetAndIterateSubchunks` calls pass as name
arguments: `0x8003B370`, `0x8003B37C`, `0x8003B388`, `0x8003B398`. Applying
the offline-derived bias to the four matching ROM offsets
(`explo2_IMGS`=`0x3bf70`, `explo_tex`=`0x3bf7c`, `explo2hi_IMGS`=`0x3bf88`,
`explh_tex`=`0x3bf98`) reproduces those exact four addresses byte-for-byte.
Two independently-derived methods (symbol-file cross-reference; disassembly
operand extraction) agree exactly — this closes the mapping question CLAUDE.md's
two-source rule requires, not a single-source guess.

**Discriminating result (why this is a real test, not just infrastructure):**
applying the same bias to the full explosion-texture table places every
entry in `0x8003B370`-`0x8003B3EC` — **~20.3 MB away** from the corrupted
read range (`arrayBase=0x801714D0`, hits at `0x80171D50`-`0x80172548`,
s122/s126). `loadExplosionTextures`/`loadAssetAndIterateSubchunks`'s own
indexing (read directly, `funcs_13.c`) only ever adds small fixed offsets
(0-0x1C) to these bases — there is no plausible index/stride bug in this
function that reaches 20 million bytes away. Combined with step 1's "zero
literal matches" result for the digit-suffixed fragments (`explo_tex2`,
`x7`-`x11`, etc. — these look like a runtime-*constructed* name+index
string, not anything stored verbatim in ROM), **this refutes "the voice
array is aliasing/indexing into this — or any — static compile-time ROM
string literal table"** as the mechanism, closing off the literal reading
of NEXT.md's "find the table-builder" framing (there is no compile-time
table close enough to be reached by any small-index bug).

**Reframes Thread B, doesn't close it.** This is consistent with, and
sharpens, s120's already-established mechanism (not overturned, reinforced):
the corrupted-index scan reads *past* the voice array's own `voiceCount`
into whatever heap allocation happens to sit adjacent to it at
`0x80171D50`+ — s122/s123 already tested and refuted the one *specific*
adjacent-allocation candidate that was checked (`loadAssetAndIterateSubchunks`'s
own DMA buffer, `ptr=0x8062B850`, ~5.87 MB away, H2 closed 3/3 per rule 8).
This session's result narrows further: whatever heap buffer actually is
adjacent is very likely also *runtime-constructed* (matches the
digit-suffixed shape), not a copy of any static ROM table — so the next
useful move is finding *which* `rs_malloc` call lands its buffer physically

data.** First soak (`rsmalloc1`, full regen + build, clean) produced
17962 `[rs-malloc]` lines whose `size` field was implausible: 59% read
`size=0`, and the nonzero remainder clustered into exactly 7 values

for a general allocator serving asset loads and DMA buffers alike. Source-read
`rs_malloc`'s body between entry and `L_80001B44` before trusting the soak
further (per this thread's own established discipline) and found the
argument order was backwards from what the patch assumed: `$a0`
(`ctx->r4`) is the size — confirmed by the very next lines rounding it
`(a0+0xF)&~0xF`, a textbook 16-byte-alignment idiom — and `$a1`
(`ctx->r5`, what the patch had captured as "size") is a **pool-selector
flags word**, tested via `&0x4`/`&0x10` to choose among three heap globals
at `0x8011xxxx`. Fixed the capture (now reads `ctx->r4` for size, logs
`ctx->r5` separately as `flags`), full regen + rebuild (clean), re-soak.

distribution** (1024, 24, 40, 72, 520, 28, 4104, 60, 32768, 356, 4096, …,
17651 total calls) and directly confirms the fix: the allocation immediately
preceding each `[song-array-alloc]` line now reports a size matching
`voiceCount * 136` exactly for all 4 song-loads this run (`voiceCount=17`→
`size=2312`, `=15`→`2040`, `=18`→`2448` ×2) — establishing the voice
array's per-slot stride as **136 bytes (0x88)**, not previously measured.
Both soaks died identically to the tracked `do_rom_read`/`piDmaWorker`
corruption SIGSEGV (hold+13s and hold+11s respectively — 3rd/4th
consecutive recurrence across the last 2 sessions' render/malloc-guard
soaks, reinforcing s137's "clear plurality" framing) — not informative on
its own, already-tracked.

corruption hits (positive control, arrayBase=0x801714D0 again), all while
the array's *own* allocation was the `voiceCount=15` one (`size=2040`,
buffer ends `0x80171CD8`).** The hit addresses (`idx=0x10`→`0x80171D50`,
`idx=0x11`→`0x80171DD8`) are **2176 and 2312 bytes past the array's own
start — both past its actual 2040-byte malloc'd length.** This is a
sharper, more literal confirmation of s120's mechanism than any prior
session had: the read isn't just past a *count* field, it's provably past
the buffer's own allocated byte extent, established directly from this
run's own size log rather than inferred.

every `[rs-malloc] ptr/size` pair by allocation order and checked which
ones' `[ptr, ptr+size)` range covers `0x80171D50`-`0x80172548` (offline

branch hoped, but a **short, closed list of exactly 3 candidates**, all
allocated once at or near boot and never returned by `rs_malloc` again
for the rest of the run (checked by grepping every later `[rs-malloc] ptr=`
line for these 3 exact pointers — zero hits, so if freed they were never
handed back out): `ptr=0x8016FD20 size=8568` (line 66, immediately after

reallocations but never freed-and-reused elsewhere per the same check).
All three sit in the same `~0x8016D000`-`0x80179000` heap region as the
voice array itself, all requested through the same `flags=0x0` pool.
`caller_ra=0x00000000` on all 17651 logged calls (100%, not just a
sample) — extends s92's "universal-zero, not corruption-specific" finding
to a 4th independent entry log, so this field stays unusable for identifying
which function called `rs_malloc` and should not be re-litigated as evidence
of anything.

**Tried one more cheap, no-rebuild step before stopping**: grepped the
recompiled C for the 3 candidates' sizes as hex literals (`0X2178`,
`0X1E30`, `0X8000`) hoping to find a call site setting the size as an
immediate constant the way `os_message_related` boilerplate sometimes
does. No real hits (the one `0X2178` match was an unrelated `MEM_W` stack

common a bit-mask constant to be useful). Confirms these sizes are
runtime-computed (consistent with the array's own `voiceCount*136`
pattern) — a literal grep cannot identify the caller; only an `rs_free`

lesson: this codebase's `rs_malloc` has `(size, flags)` argument order,
not `(pool/size, size)` as assumed by analogy with libc `malloc` — any

     for the rest of the function; at `:2624/2630/2634` it loads the
     toggle byte at `-0x68FE` (`0x80149702`), shifts it `<<2`, indexes
     into the base, and dereferences (`lw $t0, 0x0($v0)`) — reading
     whichever slot the toggle currently selects, then uses the result to
     index voice-active-flag bytes (offsets `0x85`/`0x84`/`0x0`) and as an
     argument to `musyxRenderVoiceSamples`.
   - `musyxBuildVoiceCommandList` (`funcs_24.c:2812+`): at
     `:3282-3292` loads the same toggle byte, **XORs it with 1** (selects
     the *other* slot from whichever `musyxMixActiveVoices` is using),
     computes the same `0x8015`-page base, and reads the pointer at
     either `0x80149708` or `0x8014970C` plus a companion halfword at
     `-0x68F0` (`0x80149710`) — feeding an inner call at guest
     `0x80091034`.
   - `musyxSynthFrame` (`funcs_24.c:3122+`): at `:4117-4127`, `lbu
     $v0,-0x68FE; xori $v0,$v0,1; sb $v0,-0x68FE` — **the toggle's
     writer**, flipping it every call. This is a per-VI-retrace audio
     tick (already established s101 as the function that indirectly
     calls `submitDmaRequestBatch`, the DMA-ring producer in the
     still-separately-tracked `do_rom_read` thread).
3. **Sanity check passed:** the same grep shape against `-0x6904`/
   `-0x6908` (arrayBase's own globals) returns dozens of real hits
   concentrated in the same `funcs_24.c` musyx functions — confirms the
   methodology finds genuine consumers and isn't undercounting.
4. **Bonus 2nd-source confirmation** (from `main_overlay.txt:319`,
   already used s142 for the stride fact): explicitly names
   `0x801496F8` as "the RSP-mixer voice-slot array installed by
   `initN64RspMixer`... stride 0x88" — reconfirms arrayBase's identity,
   no equivalent name exists for the `0x80149708`/`0x8014970C` pair in
   that file (0 hits either session).

**Interpretation:** this closes the "who is candidate B's consumer"
question s142 opened, but it does *not* close Thread B overall — it
reframes it. The two candidate buffers are the same 136-byte stride and
the same `N*(voiceCount+1)` sizing as the arrayBase voice array the
corruption is known to hit at a fixed `+0x34` offset (s104 on). Whether
either consumer's own indexing math into these buffers ever reaches that
same `+0x34` offset, and whether the toggle can desync from the two
`rs_malloc` calls' completion (one is a straight allocation, the other a
reload of the same halfword — s142), is now the open, source-readable
question — not more grepping for an unlocated consumer.

lines needed to identify the access pattern — that's the next work
unit's job, scoped separately so this session's result stays a single,

## Session 144 (2026-07-27) — read both slot-buffer consumers full-body (NEXT.md's prescribed work unit): refutes "either function's own indexing reaches +0x34", finds a real unchecked-cursor bug instead — a new, more specific Thread B hypothesis

Ran exactly the work unit s143 handed off: read `musyxMixActiveVoices`
and `musyxBuildVoiceCommandList` end-to-end in `funcs_24.c` and answer
the three prescribed questions (index bound, +0x34 access, timing
hazard). Delegated the read to a subagent (Explore, foreground) with the
full address-decode context and exact questions, per this session's
Fable-mode operating rules; spot-checked the subagent's most load-bearing
claim (the unchecked write-cursor) directly against `funcs_24.c:2610-2680`
before trusting it. No rebuild, no soak — this was declared source-read
only in NEXT.md.

**Function boundaries** (corrected from NEXT.md's estimates):
`musyxMixActiveVoices` is `funcs_24.c:2477-2811`;
`musyxBuildVoiceCommandList` is `funcs_24.c:2812-3121` (ends well before
the estimated 3300 — `musyxSynthFrame` starts at `:3122`, not after
3300).

**Finding 1 — +0x34, refuted for both functions.** Neither function's
own byte-offset arithmetic into a slot-derived, 136-byte-stride item
pointer ever computes `+0x34`. The only two `0x34` literals in either
function (`:2502-2503`, `:2795-2796`) are `$sp`-relative spill/reload of
register `$s3` in `musyxMixActiveVoices`'s prologue/epilogue — unrelated
to any voice-item struct. Field offsets actually touched against
slot-derived item bases: `0x0, 0x22, 0x7C, 0x80, 0x84` (destination,
`musyxMixActiveVoices`) and `0x0, 0x84, 0x85` (fixed source array,
`musyxMixActiveVoices`) and `0x22, 0x3C, 0x54, 0x7C, 0x84`
(`musyxBuildVoiceCommandList`). **This closes NEXT.md's headline
question: these two consumers are not the direct writer of the +0x34
corruption via their own indexing math.**

**Finding 2 — a real unchecked-cursor bug, not previously characterized.**
`musyxMixActiveVoices` writes into the toggle-selected destination slot
using a persistent **global** write-cursor at `0x80149710`/`0x80149712`
(a halfword per slot, `-0x68F0`/`-0x68EE` from the `0x8015`-page base) —
read pre-increment as the item index (`funcs_24.c:2648, :2653-2654` and
parallel sites at `:2705-2706, :2735-2736, :2753-2754, :2767-2768`),
scaled by `idx*136` (`<<4` then `+idx` then `<<3`, confirmed directly at
`:2647-2660`: `sll $a3,$v1,4; addu $a3,$a3,$v1; sll $a3,$a3,3`), then
incremented and written straight back to the same global address with
**no comparison against any voiceCount/capacity value anywhere in the
function** (increment+store confirmed directly at `:2663-2664,
:2673-2674`: `addiu $v0,$a0,0x1; sh $v0,0x0($s1)`). The only bound
governing how many times this cursor increments is a *different* global
halfword at `0x80149700` (`-0x6900`) that limits the **source**-side
scan loop over the fixed voice-state array at `0x801496F8` — re-read
fresh from the global every iteration (`:2682-2691`), not the same value
and not obviously tied to the destination buffer's own
`(voiceCount+1)*136` allocation size (that association isn't verifiable
from this file — `allocateSongChannelArray`, which sets the real
capacity, lives in `funcs_23.c`).

`musyxBuildVoiceCommandList` doesn't read the toggle or slot table
itself at all — it trusts `a0`/`a1` handed to it by its caller,
`musyxSynthFrame` (`:3281-3284` XORs the toggle to select the *other*
slot, `:3291-3292` loads that slot's raw buffer pointer as `a0`,
`:3299-3300` loads **the same per-slot cursor** at `0x80149710`/
`0x80149712` as `a1`). So `musyxBuildVoiceCommandList`'s loop bound is
literally the unchecked write-cursor `musyxMixActiveVoices` just
incremented on the *other* slot the previous tick — with, again, no
re-validation against the buffer's actual allocated size anywhere in
either function.

**Finding 3 — timing hazard confirmed present, not just hypothesized.**
No mutex/lock/barrier call exists in either function. `musyxMixActiveVoices`
re-reads the toggle byte from global memory **five separate times**
within one call (`:2488-2489, :2623-2624, :2657-2658, :2703-2704,
:2729-2730`) rather than caching it once in a local, each time
independently re-deriving "the current slot" — and the toggle is flipped
asynchronously by `musyxSynthFrame` every VI-retrace tick
(`:4116-4127` in absolute terms, i.e. the file's `musyxSynthFrame` body).
Nothing in `musyxMixActiveVoices` guarantees all five re-reads observe
the same slot selection within a single call. `musyxBuildVoiceCommandList`
has no analogous internal hazard (it never reads the toggle itself), but
inherits whatever `musyxSynthFrame`'s own toggle-read/XOR/table-lookup
sequence produces at `:3281-3300`.

**Reframing of Thread B:** the leading hypothesis is no longer "which
`rs_malloc` allocation is heap-adjacent to the voice array" (s138-s143's
framing) — it's now "does the unchecked `0x80149710`/`0x80149712`
write-cursor in `musyxMixActiveVoices` ever exceed the destination
slot's actual allocated item count, and does the resulting out-of-bounds
write land at a byte offset that could explain the observed +0x34
corruption in a *different* buffer" (the corruption's confirmed victim
is the arrayBase voice array at `0x801714D0`+, not this slot pair
directly — the connection, if real, would have to be spatial/heap-
adjacency, same as the original Thread B framing, but now with a
concrete unbounded-write mechanism instead of an unidentified writer).
This is a genuine, source-confirmed bug (unbounded index write, no
capacity check) independent of whether it explains the tracked
corruption — worth fixing/guarding regardless, per the project's pattern
of gating every characterized unguarded-access site (s99-s101 family).

**Not done, deliberately (per NEXT.md's own explicit deferral):** did
not build the toggle-desync timing instrument, and did not build an
instrument to catch the write-cursor exceeding capacity — both are
rebuild+instrument work, correctly deferred to the next session per
rule 8 (don't stack speculative work same-session as a source-read
unit).

**Landed:** nothing code-side (pure source read + one direct
spot-check, no rebuild, no soak). `PORTING-STATE.md` /
`docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md` / `scratch/agent/NEXT.md` (this write-up).

## Session 145 (2026-07-27) — landed and soaked the write-cursor-vs-capacity instrument s144 specified: refutes the write-cursor-overflow hypothesis for a live-captured corruption event, and finds the real mechanism instead — a non-atomic count-then-pointer update race in `allocateSongChannelArray`

Ran exactly the work unit s144/NEXT.md specified: found the real cursor
read/increment/store-back site by direct source read of
`musyxMixActiveVoices` (`funcs_24.c:2653-2668` — NEXT.md's own line
estimate, `~2648-2664`, was off by a few lines per this session's now-
recurring lesson that generated-`.c` line numbers never match an
estimate), and the real capacity source by direct source read of
`allocateSongChannelArray` (`funcs_23.c:10984-11043`): capacity is
computed once as `N * (voiceCount+1)` where `N` is itself a runtime
16-bit value read from `0x8014974E` (not a compile-time literal 2, as
"double-buffered" might suggest), cached at `0x80149704`, and reused
unchanged for both slots' `rs_malloc` sizes.

**Instrument landed** (`ROGUESQ_LOG_VOICE_CURSOR=1`,
`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, inserted immediately after the cursor's
own store-back instruction): logs the pre-increment cursor value
(`ctx->r4`, still live and unclobbered at that point), a freshly-read
toggle/slot byte, and a freshly-read capacity value from `0x80149704` —
independent of register state, matching this project's established
diagnostic convention. Verified it patched exactly once via grep before
building; full regen (`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` → `fixup_game_funcs.py`
once → `cmake --build`) exit 0, no new warnings.

**Soak** (`scratch/agent/run_voicecursor1.sh`, all existing family
diagnostics kept armed alongside the new one, `ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME=0`
per s93's confound finding): reached SELECT YOUR CRAFT, left into
hangar-flight, survived the full 30s hold + grace window with **0
crashes** — first fully clean run in the render-guard/Thread-B series in
several sessions (informative but secondary to the discriminating
result below).

**Positive control:** `[voice-cursor-hb]` fired only once (`n=0`,
heartbeat is every 5000) because the true fire count this run was tiny
— confirmed by cross-checking against the *existing*
`[voice-active-gate-nz]` control (same gating condition, `byte != 0`):
exactly 8 total fires, matching. Not a broken instrument; genuinely few
active-voice hits this run. Do not read "1 heartbeat line" as a weak
control in isolation — check it against a sibling counter on the same
gate, as done here.

**The discriminating result:** 0/8 `[voice-cursor-overflow]` fires
(cursor never reached capacity) — but the run's own
`[voice-active-gate-nz]` log (pre-existing, unrelated instrument on a
*different* read site in the same function) independently caught a live
corruption event in the same log window (lines 39024-39032 of
`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/voicecursor1/run.log`): `idx=0x10`/`0x11`
(16/17 decimal) read from `arrayBase=0x801714D0` with `count=0x0012` (18)
logged in the very same line, while the last-printed
`[song-array-alloc]` before this point was `voiceCount=15` (only
indices 0-14 should ever be scanned) and the *next* one
(`voiceCount=18`, matching the anomalous `count=18` already observed)
printed only afterward, at line 39034. The bytes read at those two
indices decode as ASCII: `"explo_tex2"` + padding + `0xFFFFFFFF` +
`"explx3"` at idx 0x10, and `"x10"`/`"explo_te"...`/`0xFFFFFFFF`/`"x11"`
at idx 0x11 — an **exact match** to the digit-suffixed fragments
(`explo_tex2`, `x10`, `x11`) s138 catalogued as present at runtime but
**absent from a full-ROM strings dump** (i.e. runtime-constructed, not
static data) — closing that open question: they are leftover bytes from
a **different, earlier heap allocation** (plausibly a texture-name/tag
table built by the explosion-texture subsystem, freed and its memory
recycled by `rs_malloc` for this later song's voice array), exposed
because the scan read 2-3 items past the array's true legitimate bound.

**Why my planned hypothesis is refuted for this instance:** at the exact
same moment (same heartbeat sample, `n=0`, sandwiched between two of the
corrupted `nz` log lines), the write-cursor was `cursor=0` against
`capacity=48` — nowhere near overflowing. The corruption instead traces
to the **scan/read side**, not the write-cursor: `musyxMixActiveVoices`'s
source-array scan loop re-reads its bound fresh from `0x80149700` every
iteration (confirmed directly, `funcs_24.c:2681-2696`,
`sltu`+reread-every-iteration), and `allocateSongChannelArray` writes the
**new** count to `0x80149700` (`funcs_23.c:10712-10713`) many
instructions **before** it calls `rs_malloc` and stores the new array
pointer / prints `[song-array-alloc]` (`funcs_23.c:10717-10738`) — a
non-atomic pair with no lock (s144 already confirmed no mutex exists
anywhere in this family). If `musyxMixActiveVoices` scans during that
window on a different thread (audio runs off `musyxSynthFrame` on the VI-
retrace thread, per s101), it sees the **new**, larger count against the
**still-old** array — landing past the old allocation's real bound into
whatever the allocator's free-list handed back to a still-not-yet-
initialized new buffer. `capacity=48` cross-checks exactly against the
`voiceCount=15` formula (`N=3`, `(15+1)*3=48`), independently confirming
`N=3` for this run — new information, not previously pinned to a number.

**Reframing of Thread B (again):** the write-cursor-overflow hypothesis
(s144's framing) is refuted for this captured instance, though it
remains a real, independent unguarded-write bug worth a guard regardless
(unchanged from s144). The corruption's actual mechanism is now a
**non-atomic count-then-pointer update race** in
`allocateSongChannelArray`, landing on **recycled, not-yet-reused heap
content from a prior, unrelated allocation** — not a stomp, not a
generic race, not a static-table indexing bug (all previously
considered and closed, s103/s113/s138). This is a single-occurrence,
single-source finding — a second, independent soak that reproduces the
same `idx > last-known-voiceCount` + `count` field mismatch would
confirm it as more than a one-off. The `do_rom_read`/`piDmaWorker`
corruption (the historically tracked +0x34 signature) did NOT recur
this run, so this finding covers a sibling read site (`voice+0x0`, the
scan/gate byte) in the same function, not a proven identical code path
to the +0x34 corruption — but it is strong corroborating evidence for
the same general class of bug (asynchronous, non-atomic multi-field
global state updated without a lock, read mid-update by a concurrent
scan) applying across both observed corruption byte-offsets.

## Session 147 (2026-07-27) — landed and soaked the s146-specified fix (count-write reorder in `allocateSongChannelArray`): 2/2 clean soaks, correct post-fix ordering 13/13 allocations, 0/2 `voice-active-gate-nz` corruption reads, 0/2 `do_rom_read` recurrences — one soak fully crash-free, a first for this crash family

**What ran:** implemented NEXT.md's prescribed fix — relocated the early
`voiceCount` write to the scan-bound global (`-0x6900` off `0x80150000`,
`funcs_23.c`, was `0x8008F0C8-CC`) to run *after* both pointer-store
writes (`-0x6904`, `-0x6908`, `0x8008F0E4`/`0x8008F0EC`) instead of
before them, via a new patch in `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py` (s147,
placed to run before the existing s120/s146 diagnostic-insertion patches
so their anchors still match unmodified instruction text).

**A real bug in NEXT.md's own plan, caught before building:** the
original code doesn't just write `-0x6900` once — it writes it, then
immediately *reloads* it (`0x8008F0D8-DC`, into `ctx->r3`, used later for
a `voiceCount == 0` branch at `0x8008F108`). NEXT.md's safety argument
("`ctx->r16` is never reassigned between the write and the print") only
covers the register the write's *value* comes from — it says nothing
about this second, independent dependency through the *memory location*
itself. Moving the write alone, leaving the reload in its original spot,
would have made the reload read the **previous** call's stale count
instead of the new one — silently changing the branch's behavior, a new
bug introduced by the "fix." Caught this by reading the full function
body (not just NEXT.md's line-number pointers) before writing the patch.
Fix: relocated the write *and* its dependent reload together, as a unit,
immediately adjacent (reload directly follows write, exactly as before)
— preserves the original branch semantics bit-for-bit while still moving
the whole pair to after the pointer stores. Verified in the regenerated
source (`funcs_23.c:10710-10749` post-fix) that the reload correctly
reads back the new value via the memory dependency, not a register one.

**Pipeline discipline note (self-caught mid-session):** ran
`fixup_game_funcs.py` twice in a row without a full regen between —

`after_p1_start_001` through `_005` (+0.6-1.6s post-press): still the
static SELECT YOUR CRAFT framing — "SELECT YOUR CRAFT" / "PRESS [A] FOR
CRAFT DESCRIPTION" text, X-wing on the pad, moon backdrop, R2 unit, red

`after_p1_start_010` (+2.6s): text overlay gone, camera has moved to a

same wall paneling, same moon, same X-wing pose, same R2 unit and red

surface rendering as dense parallel stripes) begin appearing at the top

`after_p1_start_022` through `hold_07` (+4.8s onward, ~9s wall time):

the last-drawn-sane-width gate (G1, s82) is holding this corrupted-but-
sane-width frame while the process is otherwise dead in the water, then
crashes.

At no point does a new location, ship exterior view, HUD, or flight
geometry appear. The hangar walls, moon, R2 unit, and red crate are
identifiable in every frame up to the freeze.

### Independent cross-check (2nd source, no new soak)

The archived `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/hold60/` directory (s76's actual
run) still has its screenshots. Read `after_p1_start_04.png`, `hold_01.
png`, and `hold_04.png` directly — the frames s76's own analysis
(`HOLD60_ANALYSIS.md`) called "hangar-flight content" and "airborne
X-wing" are the **identical scene** this session's `leavedense1` found:
same hangar bay walls (same blue/pink/teal glitch-panel pattern), same
X-wing pose and pad, same close/low camera angle. This is a second,
independent data point (a different run, different session, prior to
this soak) agreeing with this session's read.

### Third line of evidence: the crash's own backtrace

This soak's process died to a SIGBUS (signal 10), backtrace:
`menuOverlayInit` → `static_5_800C6854` (`runHangarMenuFromOverlay`) →
`static_5_800AAD9C` (`runHangarSelectionFrame`) → `static_5_800AB1C8`
(`composeNpcOrientationMatrix`). Cross-referenced against the crash
catalogue: this is the already-catalogued **12th class**
(`composeNpcOrientationMatrix`), first found s74/s95, guarded twice
already (s100's first-loop guard, `ROGUESQ_LOG_COMPOSE_NPC_GUARD`;
s126's second-loop guard, `ROGUESQ_LOG_COMPOSE_NPC_GUARD2`) — this is
its **3rd occurrence**. Both guards were armed this soak and neither
fired (0 hits across all 567 function-entry log lines, `arg_r4` only
ever `0x0`/`0x1`, both known-safe values) — the crash's actual fault
site is a **3rd, still-unlocated** unguarded dereference inside this
function, past both existing guards. Independent of the screenshot
read, this backtrace is itself evidence: every frame in it is
already-known hangar-menu-overlay code (`runHangarMenuFromOverlay`,
`runHangarSelectionFrame`, `composeNpcOrientationMatrix`) — none of it
is mission-overlay code. The crash happened while still executing the
hangar-selection menu's own per-frame logic, which is inconsistent with
having already transitioned into a mission or even a distinct
non-interactive flight cutscene driven by different overlay code.

### Conclusion

**s75/s76's "single Start leaves SELECT YOUR CRAFT into hangar-flight"
is overturned**, on three independent lines of evidence (this session's
dense capture, the archived s76 screenshots read fresh, and this
session's crash backtrace). What actually happens: the Start press
triggers an extended in-place camera path within the *same* craft-select
3D scene — camera moves to a progressively closer/lower angle — while
rendering corruption escalates (large striped/aliased degenerate
polygons), until the last-drawn gate freezes on a corrupted frame and
the process crashes to the 12th class's 3rd (new, unlocated) fault site.
Believable at s75/s76 because the title-yellow HUD text really does
disappear (a real menu-UI-left signal) and a tilted ship silhouette
against a starfield reads as "flying" — but the pre-Start static menu
already shares that same starfield/moon backdrop (s73 already noted
"camera orbits" even at rest), and the hangar walls remain visible in
every post-Start frame examined here.

This reopens "what input/sequence actually leaves SELECT YOUR CRAFT
into a mission" — not closed by s75/s76 after all. Two live
hypotheses for next session: (a) this camera path IS a genuine
launch-prep cinematic that would eventually cut to a real mission scene,
and the crash simply happens before that cut — surviving past the 12th
class's 3rd fault site is the way to find out; (b) the Start press
triggers some other in-hangar animation unrelated to mission launch, and
real mission entry needs a different, still-unfound input or sequence.

exactly one phase transition in the back half of this run — width 640,
origin **`0x006A2900`**, at t=142.4s (`run.log:71058`) — timed almost
exactly to the `hold_24`/`hold_25` frames (hold started ~t=116.6s per
the driver's own press schedule, so hold+25≈141.6s). This origin is
**not** any of the 3 previously-catalogued menu/outdoor origins
(`0x690400` outdoor, `0x6AB400` war room/craft-select, plus the boot
sequence's own `0x000280`/`0x66A500`/`0x790400`) — the first genuinely
new VI origin observed in this entire investigation. Per s48's own
caveat, VI parameters alone can't identify a scene, but a **novel**
value co-occurring with visually distinct, non-corrupted-hangar content
is a different, stronger claim than "same params, assume same scene."

**Two independent lines of evidence (visual + VI-origin) converge**: a
real, new scene began playing. Whether it is a genuine per-mission
intro cinematic (Star Wars films' movies open the same way; plausible
this game apes that per-mission) or an errant jump into replaying
boot-sequence scene-graph data (the corrupted camera path could plausibly
have wandered into stale/reused node pointers that happen to describe
the boot logo) is **not yet distinguished** — both are consistent with
what was observed. This directly **supports hypothesis (a)** from s150
("this camera path IS a genuine launch cinematic") over hypothesis (b)
("dead-end animation that never leaves hangar-selection") — the process
was NOT still executing hangar-menu code by the time of the new scene;
see crash backtrace below, which is scene-graph-render code, not
menu-specific.

### The crash that ended it

`[CRASH] caught signal 10 (Bus error: 10)`, backtrace resolves to
`processSceneNode + 7640` (appearing twice consecutively — likely
self-recursion, though the huge byte offset relative to this function's
expected small "per-node body" size per `symbol_files/main_overlay.txt`
makes a nearest-symbol misattribution plausible, same caveat as the
10th/18th classes' unconfirmed names) ← `traverseSceneGraphRecursive`
← `setupCameraMatrices` ← `static_5_800C9BF0` ← `menuOverlayInit` ←
`mainGameLoop`. `ROGUESQ_LOG_EMIT_DL_GUARD2`/`GUARD3` (which cover the
already-catalogued 14th class, `reserveAndEmitDLEntry`, whose typical
backtrace also runs through `submitSceneNodeRender`/`processSceneNode`)
were armed and **did not fire** — inconclusive whether this is the 14th
class in an inlined/misattributed form or a genuinely distinct site;
not resolved this session. `menuOverlayInit` is still in the stack at
crash time — the intro cinematic is being driven from the same
top-level function as the hangar menu (unsurprising; likely one
big per-frame dispatcher for the whole post-title flow), so its
presence doesn't by itself argue against a real scene change.

### `nm`/`otool`/`lldb` are not on the Bash allowlist and no human is present in this loop to grant approval

All three were tried and denied/require-approval with no way to satisfy
the prompt non-interactively. Wrote a from-scratch Mach-O LC_SYMTAB reader

get host-compiled function sizes and ordering directly from
`build/RogueSquadron64Recomp` — this is the tool to reach for next time
this class of question comes up, not another approval attempt.

### `processSceneNode+7640` is genuinely inside the function — not a nearest-symbol misattribution

`machoparse.py` against the built binary: `_processSceneNode` host size
**11188 bytes**, next symbol `_traverseSceneGraphRecursive`. `7640 < 11188`,
so the crash backtrace NEXT.md flagged as unconfirmed ("`+7640`... if the
real function is much smaller... the crash is almost certainly in a
different, subsequent function") is resolved the other way: the SIGBUS
really is inside `processSceneNode`'s own compiled code. Closes that open
question from s151/NEXT.md.

Bonus finding from the same symbol dump, unplanned but significant for the
still-open cinematic-vs-erroneous-jump question: `_menuOverlayInit`'s very
next host symbol is **`_getLevelIntroCrawlId`** — a real, compiled function
with a name that describes exactly the scene this investigation has been
watching (a per-level intro crawl). This is independent of the VI-origin
and visual evidence s151 already had, and points the same direction: this
is much more likely to be a genuine per-mission intro cinematic than an
erroneous jump into replayed boot scene-graph data. Not yet proven (a
function existing doesn't prove it's what's executing), but it's the
strongest evidence yet in that direction.

### Render-queue table counter-overflow hypothesis: REFUTED by direct measurement

A full read of `processSceneNode` (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c:
13759-14839`, ~1080 lines) found exactly one write matching this
investigation's established unguarded/unbounded-write signature: a
monotonic counter at guest `0x80128C6C`, used pre-increment as a `*12`
(3 words) stride index into a "ptr/scratch/owner" triple table at guest
`0x80116400` (matches the `symbol_files/main_overlay.txt` comment's table
address, though that comment's counter address, `0x80127894`, does NOT
match what the source actually reads/writes — confirmed by direct
computation of the `lui`/offset pairs, treat the symbol-file comment's
counter address as wrong), then incremented and stored back — with no
reset-per-frame, wraparound, or capacity check anywhere in the function.
Same shape as s145's independently-confirmed `musyxMixActiveVoices`
write-cursor overflow. Table capacity was not locatable in symbol_files
(unlike s145's cached-capacity global), so this could not yet be guarded
correctly — landed a diagnostic instead (`ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_RQ_COUNTER=1`,
`_scene_rq_counter_patch` in `fixup_game_funcs.py`, heartbeat every 500
fires + any-OOB-address alarm), following the s145 template.

Result: **decisively refuted**. 59000 fires across the whole run (boot
through the crawl scene), heartbeat count values bounce between small
numbers (2-50) every single sample — the counter is clearly reset every
frame, not monotonically growing — and `max` across the entire run never
exceeded **50** (vs. a table that spans at least several thousand
possible 12-byte entries by address arithmetic). 0/0 OOB-address fires.
This closes the leading hypothesis for this specific crash site; whatever
crashed `processSceneNode` at `+7640` in s151, it wasn't this.

### This soak didn't crash — it HUNG, and it looks like the s79/s80 FULL_SYNC-loss family recurring in a new window

`CRASH: 0` this run (contrast s151's SIGBUS at hold-iter 26/30). The
process was still alive at hold+43s/grace+66s when the script killed it.
The STAR WARS logo + crawl scene reproduced independently a 2nd time
(`[phase] vi_width=640 ... origin=0x006A2900 at 142.7s` — byte-identical
timing to s151's `142.4s`, strong reproducibility confirmation), and the
densified frames show real progression through the logo zoom/fade
(`hold_13`→`hold_17`) into crawl text that gets **larger and closer**
(`hold_20` pure black → `hold_21` first glyph fragments, much bigger than
s151's un-densified capture ever showed) — but by `hold_22` the visible
text is corrupted/doubled ("`S SSSSS SSSS SS`" repeating glyphs, garbled
fragments underneath), and from `hold_23` through `hold_30` (7+ seconds,
confirmed by byte-for-byte-identical screenshots at 5 Hz) the frame is
**completely frozen** — same "D..." partial-glyph frame every single
capture, no further motion. **Item 2's stretch goal (transcribe the crawl
text) is not achievable from this data**: the text isn't scrolling too
fast to capture, it's rendering corrupted (doubled/repeating glyphs)
before it freezes, so no tick rate would have resolved it.

The `run.log` explains the freeze: `[vi] update_screen` keeps incrementing
normally through `#10624` (VI/present loop still alive, still swapping
between two origins `0x00644D00`/`0x006A2900`) but **`fs` (RDP task/
FULL_SYNC count) is flat at `3527` for the entire tail of the log** — RDP
work stopped completing while VI kept re-presenting the last real frame.
This is the exact `fs`-plateau-with-live-VI signature s79/s80 already
characterized and root-caused as a class ("M3 blocker = post-leave
FULL_SYNC loss") for a *different* window (the hangar-leave transition,
~90s scene). Finding the same signature here — a different scene,
~50s later in wall-clock time — reframes this from "a new, unrelated
hang" to **a likely recurrence of the already-partially-understood
FULL_SYNC-loss class**, not a fresh mystery requiring a new investigation
thread from scratch. The already-known secondary symptom
(`UnhandledJumpTarget 0x0231` in `factor5_ucode`, called out at s79 as
"secondary, not onset cause") also recurred here, 876 times — consistent
with, not proof of, the same-mechanism reading.

### Conclusion / next steps

Do not re-chase "find a table-deref site to guard" in `processSceneNode`
next — that specific hypothesis (this function's own render-queue counter)
is refuted, and this session found no crash at all to localize a guard
against. The higher-value thread now is the `fs`-plateau: re-run s80's
`[vi-fs-decision]` diagnostic (already characterized for the hangar-leave
window) across this crawl-scene window to test whether it's genuinely the
same mechanism, and/or extend `HOLD_S` well past 30 (this run's capture
window ended while the process was still alive but frozen — unknown
whether it ever recovers on a longer hold). Full detail above.

### Part 1 result: CONFIRMED, same class as s79/s80

`grep vi-fs-decision scratch/s73_post_a_scene/scenerq1/run.log` shows
`rdpFs` (the RDP FULL_SYNC-opcode counter) first reaching its final value
`3527` at decision `#9049` (`synth=962`) and staying pinned at `3527`
through the last line in the file, decision `#10624` (`synth=1491`) —
**529 more synthetic `FIRE reason=swap` events fired, all with `seen=0`,
after `rdpFs` stopped moving**, across roughly 1575 decisions and (per
the driver summary) the remaining ~7 seconds of the hold window. This is
exactly s80's discriminating signature ("synthetic FIRE continues after
the `fs` plateau" — i.e. the driver keeps deciding a real framebuffer swap
happened and firing the synthetic completion path, even though the RDP
genuinely stopped completing tasks). Bonus observation not in s80's
original write-up: right at the plateau onset the fired pairs' `lastCimg`
values are sane (`0x006A2400`/`0x00644800`, matching the two VI origins
in play, `lastW=640`), but by the end of the log `lastCimg`/`lastW` have
drifted into clearly wild values (`0x00FE7xxx`/`0x00AE03F1` with widths
like `1`, `97`, `4083`) — consistent with s81's "mode-3 present of wild
last-drawn" characterization of the visual symptom, now shown to extend
into this window too. **Conclusion: this is confirmed (not just
suggestive) the same FULL_SYNC-loss class as s79/s80, recurring in the
crawl-scene window rather than a distinct bug.** Upgrades s152's
single-soak S1-grade suggestion to a same-run, two-independent-line
confirmation (signature match + no counter-example anywhere in the log).

The `run_extendhold1` soak never reached the crawl-scene window at all.
It crashed at wall-clock **74.1s** (hold-iter 3, ~2s into the 120s hold
window) — long before s152's soak reached the `142s` crawl scene, and
still inside the war-room/craft-select region (`last phase` line shows
`vi_width=512 origin=0x006AB400`). Backtrace:
`processSceneNode+7176 ← submitSceneNodeRender ← traverseSceneGraphRecursive
← setupCameraMatrices ← static_5_800AAD9C ← static_5_800C6854 ←
menuOverlayInit`, SIGBUS. This is **inside the same function as s151's
`processSceneNode+7640` crash** (confirmed real, s152's `machoparse.py`
measurement: function is 11188 bytes host-compiled, both offsets are
within it) but at a **different offset and a different call path**
(`submitSceneNodeRender` vs. whatever chain led to s151's site — not
recorded in enough detail last session to compare directly). Given this
family's already-documented extreme session-to-session crash-class
variability (NEXT.md's own carried-forward note, ~20 sessions), this
reads as another data point in that variability, not evidence the
`+7640` and `+7176` sites are the same bug — they're close enough in the
same function to plausibly share the unguarded-table-deref shape common
to every other guarded class in this investigation, but that's
unconfirmed, not measured this session. **Item 2's actual question (does
the crawl-scene `fs` plateau ever recover on a long hold) is still

## Session 154 (2026-07-27) — re-ran the extended-hold soak (2nd of 3 allowed attempts) — this time it reached the crawl scene, the RDP `fs` plateau **recovered on its own mid-run**, and the game rendered the furthest-ever new content (a planet-horizon shot then a ship silhouette, cinematic-shaped) before dying to a brand-new, unrelated 20th crash class

### What ran

Exactly NEXT.md's prescribed retry: moved s153's `extendhold1/` capture
dir aside (`extendhold1_s153`), reran `scratch/agent/run_extendhold1.sh`
unchanged (`HOLD_S=120`, same instrument battery), blocked on the process
exiting, then read `run.log`'s `[vi-fs-decision]` tail the way s153 did.

### Found

**The freeze recovers.** This run reached the crawl scene
(`[phase] vi_width=640 (was 512) origin=0x006A2900 at 141.4s
update_screen #8483`, same origin s151-s153 already tied to the intro
cinematic) and initially reproduced the exact s152/s153 signature:
`rdpFs` (RDP FULL_SYNC opcode count) plateaus at **3516**, holding flat
across decisions **#8970 through #9656** (686 consecutive
`[vi-fs-decision]` entries, all `FIRE reason=swap`, synthetic swaps
firing the whole time with `rdpFs` never moving — the identical
"synthetic FIRE continues after `fs` plateau" shape s80/s152/s153
characterized). Unlike every prior observation of this signature,
**this run did not stay stuck**: by decision **#10912**, `rdpFs` had
moved to **4142**, and it kept climbing steadily all the way to
**5607** at the moment of the eventual crash (`fs max: 5607` in the
soak summary, confirmed via a dense per-decision dump — no further
plateau after the recovery point). This directly answers NEXT.md's open
question: **the FULL_SYNC-loss state is not a permanent stall in at
least this instance** — it is a transient condition the run recovered
from unassisted, after being stuck for roughly 686 decisions (out of
~10600 total in the log).

**Bonus, unplanned — furthest content ever reached.** The screenshots
across the plateau/recovery window show *why* `fs` resumed: the game
was still progressing through cinematic content the whole time, just
not draining the RDP queue for a stretch. `hold_45/60/85.png` (before
and during the plateau) are pure black. `hold_90.png` — taken during
the climb from 3516 toward 5607 — is a **new scene never seen before in
this investigation**: a curved planetary horizon against black space,
composed exactly like the iconic *Star Wars* opening establishing shot.
`hold_95.png` and `hold_101.png` (the last frame before death) show a
second new scene: a fan of dark radiating lines converging on a bright
white wedge with a dark red/black shape at the right edge — read as an
engine-glow/ship-silhouette shot, consistent with a Star-Destroyer-style
flyover matching the "AMBUSH AT MOS EISLEY" mission's Tatooine setting.
Both scenes are geometrically coherent (no corruption, no garbage
colors) — a different, cleaner failure mode than every prior post-leave
scene in this investigation. This is the first time the process has
rendered content past the crawl text at all.

**New, 20th crash class.** The run ultimately died (`CRASH: 1`, hold-
iter 102/120, `hold done wall=111s`) to a SIGBUS with a backtrace never
seen before in ~154 sessions:

```
loadCraftShadowTextures + 612
 <- allocateAndInitCraftNpcContext + 564
 <- static_6_800A7C4C + 10756
 <- load_cutscene + 4300
 <- cinematicLoopBody + 3160
 <- mainGameLoop + 5220
```

Grepped both docs for every symbol in this backtrace — zero prior hits.
This is a distinct call chain from the `processSceneNode`/
`submitSceneNodeRender`/`traverseSceneGraphRecursive` family that every
crawl-scene/craft-select crash so far (s151, s153) has shared; it is
also distinct from the guarded hangar-tick family (composeNpcOrientation
Matrix, projectModelBoundsToScreen, etc.) and from the tracked `do_rom_
read`/DMA-ring race. `load_cutscene` and `cinematicLoopBody` are new
names in this investigation's vocabulary — consistent with the game
having moved from the crawl into an actual mission-intro cutscene
(craft/NPC shadow-texture loading is exactly what a cinematic establishing
shot would trigger). Not source-read this session — 1 occurrence, not
yet root-caused, catalogued per the standing convention (the retracted
"20th" from s116/s126 leaves this number free; s99-101's unguarded-
table-deref shape has not been confirmed here, this is a fresh site).

### What this rules out / reframes

- Refutes reading the s79/s80/s152/s153 "`fs` plateau + synthetic FIRE
  continues" signature as an unconditional permanent hang — it is a
  slow patch, not necessarily terminal. Future observations of the same
  signature should not be assumed stuck without watching `rdpFs` over a
  longer window first.
- Reframes the crawl-scene investigation: the blocker to reaching
  further mission content is **not** primarily the FULL_SYNC-loss state
  (which resolved itself here) but the crash-class gauntlet — this run
  got further than any before specifically because it survived long
  enough for the plateau to clear on its own, then died to an unrelated,
  new bug once genuinely new content (the cutscene) started exercising
  code paths (texture/NPC-context allocation for a cutscene) this
  investigation had never reached before.
- Does not tell us whether the recovery is reliable/reproducible (n=1)
  or was itself luck (e.g., some other counter crossing a threshold).
  Don't generalize "it always recovers" from one instance.

### Next work unit

Per NEXT.md's own plan, the immediate next step is to characterize the
new 20th class (`loadCraftShadowTextures`/`allocateAndInitCraftNpcContext`)
the same way s99-s101 characterized the hangar-tick family: source-read
first (find the exact host file/offsets via `machoparse.py` against
`symbol_files/`), confirm whether it's the same unguarded-table-deref
shape, and guard it if so. This is now the standing blocker to reaching
further into the mission-intro cutscene, since the `fs`-plateau question
that motivated the last 3 sessions is provisionally answered (recovers,
at least once).
